content:
Hello everyone!

I recently graduated with a bachelors in math and philosophy from Lawrence University with plans to study math in grad school. I'm new to Lean (like just finished the Natural Number Game new) but hopefully can contribute to mathlib down the road. I've particularly enjoyed learning differential geometry and have a side interest in physics, but I don't want to specialize too quickly. Alongside Lean, I'm studying Galois theory at a leisurely pace.

Due to a constant state of running out of disk space I'm exclusively using codespace to go through Mathematics in Lean. :rolling_on_the_floor_laughing: . My goal (haha) is to get through the book before starting grad school.

Thanks all for reading :)
